q: Thurston's topological characterisation of rational maps says a branched cover f: S²→S² (finite postcritical set) is equivalent to a rational map iff:
opts: f has no Thurston obstruction (no multicurve with eigenvalue ≥1 in the Thurston matrix)
exp: Thurston rigidity (proved by Douady–Hubbard 1993): f is homotopy equivalent to a rational map iff it has no Thurston obstruction. An obstruction is an invariant multicurve Γ with λ(A_Γ)≥1. If the rational map exists, it is unique up to Möbius conjugacy.
